assertion_results.text: Data extraction correctly identifies CVE-2026-31812, library quinn-proto, affected range < 0.11.14, and fixed version 0.11.14 from the Vulnerability issue (Step 1)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md Step 1 table: CVE ID = CVE-2026-31812, Vulnerable library = quinn-proto, Affected version range = < 0.11.14, Fixed version = 0.11.14

assertion_results.text: Data extraction identifies the ecosystem as Cargo based on the library name and component context (Step 1 Ecosystem detection)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md Ecosystem Detection section: 'The vulnerable library is quinn-proto, which is a Rust crate. Based on the Ecosystem Mappings tables in the security matrix, this maps to the Cargo ecosystem.'

assertion_results.text: Version impact table includes ALL versions from the security-matrix.md supportability matrix — no versions are skipped (Important Rule 4)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md lists all 7 versions: 2.1.0, 2.1.1 (stream 2.1.x) and 2.2.0, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.3, 2.2.4 (stream 2.2.x). No versions are skipped.

assertion_results.text: Version impact analysis uses pinned commit tags from the supportability matrix for each version, not branch HEAD (Important Rule 13)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md explicitly states: 'Dependency versions are extracted from pinned commit tags in the supportability matrix (not branch HEAD), per Important Rule 13.' The Tag column shows v0.3.8, v0.3.12, v0.4.5, v0.4.8, v0.4.9, v0.4.11, v0.4.12.

assertion_results.text: Version impact table identifies retag versions and carries forward the affected status from the original version (Important Rule 5)
assertion_results.evidence: version-impact.md: '2.2.2 | 2.2.x | v0.4.9 | -- | YES | retag of 2.2.1 (same as 2.2.1, backend tag v0.4.8)' and summary: 'Retag: 2.2.2 is a retag of 2.2.1 (identical backend source commit v0.4.8); the lock file check was skipped and the affected status was carried forward from 2.2.1.'

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction proposes replacing PSIRT-assigned versions with lock-file-verified versions, showing the diff (Step 3.2)
assertion_results.evidence: affects-versions.md Step 3.2 shows: Current (PSIRT-assigned) = RHTPA 2.0.0, Proposed (lock-file-verified) = RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2. A diff-style table with rationale is provided.

assertion_results.text: Affects Versions correction references version names from the supportability matrix rather than hardcoded Jira version IDs (Important Rule 6)
assertion_results.evidence: affects-versions.md: 'Version names (RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2) are referenced from the supportability matrix rather than hardcoded Jira version IDs (Important Rule 6).' Jira IDs are placeholders (<RHTPA-2.2.0-jira-id>, etc.) resolved at runtime.

assertion_results.text: Remediation tasks include Repository, Target Branch, acceptance criteria, and dependency linkage between upstream and downstream tasks (Important Rule 9)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md Task 1: Repository = backend, Target Branch = release/0.4.z, Acceptance Criteria with checkboxes, Dependencies section. Task 2: Repository = rhtpa-release.0.4.z, Target Branch = main, Acceptance Criteria, Dependencies. Blocks link between upstream and downstream specified in Proposed Jira Linkage section.

assertion_results.text: For Cargo ecosystem, remediation creates two tasks: upstream backport task and downstream propagation subtask with Blocks dependency (Important Rule 8)
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md: 'Task 1: Upstream Backport Task' and 'Task 2: Downstream Propagation Subtask'. Linkage section specifies 'Upstream task -> Downstream task (Blocks): jira.create_link(inwardIssue: <upstream-task-key>, outwardIssue: <downstream-task-key>, type: "Blocks")'

assertion_results.text: The analysis presents triage recommendations as proposed actions — framing Affects Versions changes, label additions, and status transitions as proposals rather than executed mutations (Guardrails)
assertion_results.evidence: Multiple notes throughout: data-extraction.md: 'Note: No Jira operations were performed. These are proposed actions only.' affects-versions.md: 'Note: No Jira operations were performed. These are proposed actions only.' remediation.md: 'No Jira operations were performed. All remediation tasks, links, transitions, labels, and comments are presented as proposed actions rather than executed mutations.'

assertion_results.text: The data-extraction output describes Step 0.7 actions before the Step 1 data table: assigning the CVE issue to the current user and transitioning it to Assigned status (Step 0.7)
assertion_results.evidence: data-extraction.md begins with 'Step 0.7 -- Early Assignment (Proposed)' describing: 1) 'Assign the CVE issue to the current user' via jira.edit_issue, 2) 'Transition to Assigned status' via jira.transition_issue. This appears before the 'Step 1 -- Data Extraction' section.

assertion_results.text: Release orchestration preserves interactive confirmation of the exact release Epic version and separate child Task creation; when release evidence or confirmation is unavailable, it reports pending work instead of claiming creation.
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md Step 7.5: Shows interactive Epic version confirmation prompt with 3 options (Accept, Specify different version, Skip). Step 7.5.2 shows separate Task creation confirmation. Final note: 'Since release evidence and confirmation are unavailable in this evaluation, this is reported as pending work rather than claiming creation.'

assertion_results.text: Release dedup is skipped when its Upstream Affected Component configuration is absent. When trusted release evidence is available, the proposed procedure resolves originating CVEs through Blocks/Depend links, compares their components and allows library-summary fallback only for a missing Depend link or component field; a known nonmatch does not count as dedup, and unavailable release evidence is not fabricated.
assertion_results.evidence: remediation.md Step 7.5.3: 'The Upstream Affected Component custom field is not configured in Security Configuration. Per the methodology, when the Upstream Affected Component custom field is absent, Step 7.5.3 dedup is skipped entirely. No dedup check is performed.' No release evidence is fabricated.
